biography.plain_text: Simon Hume-Kendall is a British entrepreneur whose career spans shipping, hotels and leisure. He founded Tower Heritage Hotels in 1985 and sold its seven-property chain in 1991, later building and selling Kent's Hop Farm and associated businesses. His public-company work included shipping groups, energy ventures and the chairmanship of AIM Investments.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before moving into tourism, Hume-Kendall worked with shipping groups including Seascope, Norex and Appledore, and later became involved in Burren Energy. He broadened his activities into Kent tourism, combining accommodation, visitor attractions and waterside enterprises. Lamberhurst Vineyard and the Bewl Water operations contributed to his recognition as a regional entrepreneur.

AIM Investments appointed him as non-executive chairman. He also served on boards in media, finance and sport, including Sport Media Group and Crystal Palace Football Club. Subsequent ventures extended into holiday property, power and software. Hume-Kendall disposed of the Hop Farm group in 2008.
